    <div class="content-inner">

    <div class="headline">Sun Country Airlines: Customer Segmentation</div>

    <div class="project-meta-block">
      <p class="project-meta-line">UC Irvine &middot; MSBA Coursework</p>
      <p class="project-meta-line">06/2026-07/2026</p>
    </div>

    <p class="body-text"><strong>Project Context:</strong> Sun Country Airlines, a Minneapolis-based low-cost leisure carrier operating out of MSP (Minneapolis-Saint Paul International Airport), had no dedicated data analyst on staff and relied entirely on anecdotal assumptions to drive marketing decisions. Acting as an analytics consultant for a BANA 200 case study, I applied K-Means clustering, a machine learning technique that groups similar customers together, to 15,144 customer-trip records spanning 2013 to 2014, identifying five actionable segments and translating the findings into three targeted campaigns tied to leadership's stated goals around Ufly loyalty enrollment, direct channel growth, and vacation package differentiation.</p>

    <p class="body-text"><strong>Business Question:</strong> <em>Which distinct customer segments exist within Sun Country's booking data, and what targeted strategies should the airline pursue to grow loyalty enrollment, increase direct bookings, and differentiate its vacation packages?</em></p>

    <div class="mobile-deliverables">
      <a class="mobile-deliverable-btn" href="report.pdf" target="_blank">Full Report &rarr;</a>
      <a class="mobile-deliverable-btn" href="slides.pdf" target="_blank">Slides &rarr;</a>
      <a class="mobile-deliverable-btn" href="code.html" target="_blank">Code &rarr;</a>
    </div>

    <div class="tabs">
      <button class="tab-btn active" onclick="showTab('segments', this)">The 5 Customer Segments</button>
      <button class="tab-btn" onclick="showTab('findings-recs', this)">Findings &amp; Recommendations</button>
      <button class="tab-btn" onclick="showTab('methodology-takeaways', this)">Methodology &amp; Takeaways</button>
    </div>

    <!-- THE 5 CUSTOMER SEGMENTS -->
    <div id="segments" class="tab-panel active">

      <p class="prose" style="margin-top:0.25rem;">K-Means with k=5 revealed five distinct, business-interpretable groups. The clearest pattern: Clusters 0 and 1 share the same Minneapolis leisure traveler profile but split entirely on where they book, direct versus third-party platforms like Expedia. Loyalty enrollment was almost entirely absent outside Cluster 3.</p>
      <div class="segment-grid">
        <div class="segment-card seg-0">
          <div class="segment-name">C0: MSP Direct Bookers</div>
          <div class="segment-pct">27.3%</div>
          <div class="segment-desc">MSP locals booking on SCA.com. 74% direct channel. 99.9% not enrolled in Ufly, the single largest loyalty opportunity.</div>
        </div>
        <div class="segment-card seg-1">
          <div class="segment-name">C1: MSP Deal Seekers</div>
          <div class="segment-pct">25.4%</div>
          <div class="segment-desc">Same traveler as C0 but 100% third-party channel. A margin problem with a structural fix.</div>
        </div>
        <div class="segment-card seg-2">
          <div class="segment-name">C2: Inbound Visitors</div>
          <div class="segment-pct">16.1%</div>
          <div class="segment-desc">95% fly into Minneapolis. Low spend, one-way dominant, 95% non-Ufly.</div>
        </div>
        <div class="segment-card seg-3">
          <div class="segment-name">C3: Loyal Frequent Fliers</div>
          <div class="segment-pct">15.7%</div>
          <div class="segment-desc">99% Ufly Standard. Highest ticket spend and longest booking lead time of any segment.</div>
        </div>
        <div class="segment-card seg-4">
          <div class="segment-name">C4: Returning Home Fliers</div>
          <div class="segment-pct">15.5%</div>
          <div class="segment-desc">98% flying home to MSP. 30% already hold Ufly Standard, a natural vacation package target.</div>
        </div>
      </div>

      <p class="prose">Two numbers from the initial exploratory analysis (EDA) foreshadowed everything the clustering later confirmed: 78.5% of customers weren't enrolled in Ufly Rewards, Sun Country's loyalty program, and bookings split almost evenly between direct (45.9%, via SCA.com) and third-party channels (44.0%, Expedia and similar).</p>

    </div>

    <!-- FINDINGS & RECOMMENDATIONS -->
    <div id="findings-recs" class="tab-panel">

      <div class="rec-card high">
        <div class="rec-priority">High Priority</div>
        <div class="rec-title">Launch Direct Booking + Ufly Enrollment Campaign</div>
        <div class="rec-segment">C0 + C1 &middot; 52.7% of customers</div>
        <div class="rec-desc">C0 already books direct but isn't enrolled, a post-booking miles bonus fixes that cheaply. C1 books entirely through third parties, so a 5-10% direct-booking discount gives them a reason to switch before the enrollment prompt.</div>
      </div>

      <div class="rec-card med">
        <div class="rec-priority">Medium Priority</div>
        <div class="rec-title">Introduce a Ufly Elite Tier</div>
        <div class="rec-segment">C3 &middot; 15.7% of customers</div>
        <div class="rec-desc">C3 is 99% Ufly Standard with the highest spend and no status tier to aspire toward. Gating perks like priority boarding behind a spend threshold protects this loyalty before a competitor's status-match does.</div>
      </div>

      <div class="rec-card med">
        <div class="rec-priority">Medium Priority</div>
        <div class="rec-title">Cross-Sell Vacation Packages at Checkout</div>
        <div class="rec-segment">C4 &middot; 15.5% of customers</div>
        <div class="rec-desc">C4 flies home one-way with existing Ufly affinity. An outbound "plan your next escape" prompt at checkout converts one-way buyers into round-trip vacation customers.</div>
      </div>

      <div class="rec-card low">
        <div class="rec-priority">Lower Priority</div>
        <div class="rec-title">Test a Round-Trip Bundle Offer</div>
        <div class="rec-segment">C2 &middot; 16.1% of customers</div>
        <div class="rec-desc">The most transactional, lowest-spend segment. Worth testing, but not a core focus given limited brand attachment.</div>
      </div>

    </div>

    <!-- METHODOLOGY & TAKEAWAYS -->
    <div id="methodology-takeaways" class="tab-panel">

      <div class="section-heading" style="margin-top:0.25rem;">Methodology</div>
      <ul class="findings-list">
        <li><strong>Data prep:</strong> started with 15,144 records across 90 features, removed two identifier columns with no analytical signal, worked with pre-normalized data and no missing values.</li>
        <li><strong>EDA:</strong> surfaced the near-even booking channel split and the 78.5% non-Ufly rate before any model ran, both of which shaped how every cluster was later interpreted.</li>
        <li><strong>Choosing k=5:</strong> tested k=2 through 10 using the Elbow Method (plotting error against cluster count and looking for where more clusters stop helping) and Silhouette Score (how cleanly each customer fits its cluster), both pointed to k=5 as the best balance of statistical fit and business interpretability.</li>
      </ul>

      <div class="section-heading">Takeaways</div>
      <ul class="findings-list">
        <li>The channel split between C0 and C1 was the most strategically interesting finding, two nearly identical traveler profiles that needed two completely different interventions.</li>
        <li>Naming segments mattered. Personas like "MSP Direct Bookers" made the results usable for stakeholders who'd never read a centroid table.</li>
        <li>Unsupervised learning runs on judgment, not accuracy scores. Deciding how many clusters to use and what a centroid means in business terms is where the real analytical work happens.</li>
      </ul>

    </div>
